what_was_wrong: The E2E runtime intentionally boots with no paired-host credential, but AgentChatProvider required PairedHostState to be connected even when pairedHost.host was null. Its initial unpaired state therefore disabled Create chat and stalled every legacy fake-engine flow.
The session-detail route also treated paired-host state as mandatory in direct-web mode and could leave an already-selected paired session rendered after the paired Mac became unreachable.
Every SSE retry failure could request another paired-host refresh, coupling the reconnect loop to repeated health probes.
Every successful cadence probe also rebuilt the paired client object, which could restart the SSE effect and its recovery refreshes every five seconds even though the host had not changed.
The new Playwright cases used exact tab names that did not match the icon-prefixed accessible names and did not consistently account for Expo Router's hidden duplicate mounts.
The fake mobile gateway needed an explicit healthy reachability default so a reset never depended on a prior control request.
what_changed: Paired-host reachability gates OpenCode/chat behavior only when pairedHost.host exists; unpaired web/E2E sessions continue to derive availability from the direct OpenCode connection.
The bounded health refresh returns immediately without a host, and AppState/polling probes only start for a persisted paired host.

Paired session and Agents routes render the authoritative paired-host offline state before any loaded-session or spinner branch; unpaired connection failures retain the original OpenCode offline fallback.
The SSE loop reports one paired reachability failure per outage and resets that guard only after receiving a real event.
The paired client is stable for the same account, host, device, and gateway scope, so successful health polling cannot restart SSE.
Fake-server state resets to mobileReachability=online, and its control endpoint can switch paired gateway traffic to error or timeout modes.
The c3, mutations, and c5 cases use visible-filtered locators and exact or end-anchored, non-substring accessible names.
The c5 recovery case asserts one visible final transcript line and unique Activity item IDs after reconnect.
